sources.entry: Bye AppQuit - A minimal menu bar app to quickly view and kill running processes. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/designsbymuzeer/Bye-Mac-App) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
Bye-AppQuit - A minimal native macOS app to quickly view and Bulk kill running processes.

summary.one_liner: Bye is a small, open-source native macOS menu bar app, built with SwiftUI, that quits running applications in bulk with one click.
summary.what_it_does: The app lives in the macOS menu bar and shows a popover listing running apps. A single click quits all running user applications at once. Individual apps can be selected or deselected so they stay open. It uses SwiftUI for the interface and AppKit's NSWorkspace for process management. The README says it has a glass-morphic look that adapts to Light and Dark Mode. On first run it installs a background service that monitors application changes.
use_cases: quit all open apps at once on a Mac
bulk close running applications from the menu bar
selectively quit apps while keeping some open
reclaim system focus after closing many apps
how_to_run: Download the latest Bye.zip from the Releases page
On first run, right-click the app and select Open to bypass the unidentified developer warning
To build from source: open Bye.xcodeproj in Xcode (macOS 14.5+)
Build and run with Cmd + R
notable: Menu bar utility for bulk-quitting running apps
Select or deselect apps to keep them open
Glass-morphic UI that adapts to Light and Dark Mode
Built only with Apple's native frameworks, no third-party dependencies named
Open source with full source code in the repository
caveats: Not notarized or on the Mac App Store, so macOS shows an unidentified developer warning on first open
Requires macOS 13.0 (Ventura) or newer; building from source needs Xcode on macOS 14.5+
Versions released after Nov 27, 2025 are GPLv3 licensed (the README also states the project is GPLv3)
